notes: Repro (MATLAB after initCobraToolbox, gurobi): m = createModel({'EX_A';'R1';'R2';'BIO'}, {'EX_A';'R1';'R2';'BIO'}, {' -> A';'A -> B';'A -> B';'B -> '}, 'upperBoundList', [10 1000 1000 1000], 'grRuleList', {'';'1.1';'10.1';''}, 'printLevel', 0); m = changeObjective(m, 'BIO'); [~, ko, ~, ~, del] = singleGeneDeletion(m, 'FBA', [], false, 1) -> ko = [0 10], del{1} = {'R1';'R2'}; non-unique call singleGeneDeletion(m, 'FBA', {'1.1';'10.1'}) gives [10 10]. The defect is confined to the call form uniqueGene = 1 on a model whose genes carry transcript suffixes (.N) and where one gene identifier is a prefix of another (e.g. Entrez 1 and 10, common in Recon models): callers that pass uniqueGene = 1 reach it, the others (default 0) do not. Existing multi-function legacy test testDeletionStudy.m (singleGeneDeletion/doubleGeneDeletion/singleRxnDeletion) also calls it, not renamed. Further observations (not recorded as defects): line 77 'grRateWT = solWT.f' has no semicolon (prints grRateWT in the uniqueGene branch, cosmetic); in the uniqueGene branch a gene without effect or an infeasible knock-out leaves a zero flux column (non-unique branch: wild type flux / NaN), not probed.
